2c699b8a3618269d5834d262c0f297191630f1a5.abstract: Identifying conditions that a certain drug takes therapeutic effect on a target disease is crucial for clinical decision-making support. However, most existing biomedical information extraction methods have focused on identifying only relations between drugs and diseases, while largely overlooking the context-specific conditions where such relations can apply. We create the first dataset that has manually annotated triples of drugs, diseases, and applicability conditions on biomedical paper abstracts with 1,119 drug-disease pairs. However, existing benchmarks predominantly focus on static evaluation, assessing models on isolated data points. This approach neglects a critical aspect of clinical practice: longitudinal analysis, where physicians interpret patient data as a dynamic trajectory to track disease progression and treatment response. 262328c2d864b921cfa0616e952e5c84cc5f02a8.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong performance and rapid progress in a wide range of medical reasoning tasks. However, their sequential autoregressive decoding forces inherently parallel clinical reasoning, such as differential diagnosis, into a single linear reasoning path, limiting both efficiency and reliability for complex medical problems. To address this, we propose MedVerse, a reasoning framework for complex medical inference that reformulates medical reasoning as a parallelizable directed acyclic graph (DAG) process based on Petri net theory. The framework adopts a full-stack design across data, model architecture, and system execution. 20a80d5110424ad9701858691cd857f6f48cedc9.title: How Robust Are Large Language Models for Clinical Numeracy? An Empirical Study on Numerical Reasoning Abilities in Clinical Contexts
20a80d5110424ad9701858691cd857f6f48cedc9.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for clinical question answering and decision support, yet safe deployment critically requires reliable handling of patient measurements in heterogeneous clinical notes. 1a9b8de7688dbb5f3049f5bc8a700502332cfc22.title: TheraAgent: Self-Improving Therapeutic Agent for Precise and Comprehensive Treatment Planning
1a9b8de7688dbb5f3049f5bc8a700502332cfc22.abstract: Formulating a treatment plan is inherently a complex reasoning and refinement task rather than a simple generation problem. However, existing large language models (LLMs) mainly rely on one-shot output without explicit verification, which may result in rough, incomplete, and potentially unsafe treatment plans. 1447859940005bfcdc2156673cf7f1bab455a0cf.abstract: In this paper we introduce ClinQueryAgent, a system for translating natural language population health questions into executable database queries using agents with access to both local and external knowledge bases. We deploy the system via a chat window embedded within an existing population health management platform where it has been used by 128 staff from 15 healthcare practices covering a total of 148,319 patients in the UK's National Health Service (NHS). 1447859940005bfcdc2156673cf7f1bab455a0cf.zh_abstract: 在本文中，我们介绍 ClinQueryAgent，一个使用可访问本地和外部知识库的智能体（agents）将自然语言人群健康问题转化为可执行数据库查询的系统。我们新颖的架构使得能够使用强大的基于云的语言模型，同时确保没有患者数据离开安全环境。为了对抗由于上下文腐化（context rot）在较长对话过程中出现的不准确，信息检索被委托给一个子智能体（sub-agent）。我们通过嵌入现有的人群健康管理平台中的聊天窗口部署该系统，该平台已被来自英国国家医疗服务体系（NHS）15 家医疗机构的 128 名工作人员使用，覆盖总计 148,319 名患者。我们在一个构建的数据集上并通过 beta 测试阶段评估该系统自主处理一系列健康信息学任务的能力。我们的结果

0ad7460e87bacd07b1f26da3ef2f2d2fdd3ea4d9.title: MSIA: Adaptive Medical Multimodal Multi-turn Semantic Jailbreak
0ad7460e87bacd07b1f26da3ef2f2d2fdd3ea4d9.abstract: Medical multimodal large language models are increasingly deployed in high-stakes clinical settings, yet current safety evaluations largely overlook a critical failure mode: covert semantic drift that accumulates across clinically plausible multi-turn interactions. Such drift can lead models to gradually exaggerate or conceal critical medical findings without triggering explicit safety mechanisms. We propose MSIA ( M edical S emantic I nfiltration A ttack), a framework for modeling and inducing multi-turn medical semantic jailbreaks in clinical dialogues. MSIA enables the controlled optimization of cumulative semantic drift under stealth constraints through adaptive strategy selection and closed-loop reward feedback grounded in medical evidence. Experiments on chest X-ray–based multimodal medical dialogues show that MSIA consistently outperforms existing jailbreak methods across GPT-4o,
0ad7460e87bacd07b1f26da3ef2f2d2fdd3ea4d9.zh_title: MSIA：医疗多模态多轮语义越狱攻击
0ad7460e87bacd07b1f26da3ef2f2d2fdd3ea4d9.summary: 提出MSIA框架，建模并诱导临床合理多轮对话中逐步累积的隐蔽语义漂移，揭示医疗多模态大模型安全评测盲区。
key_points: 指出多轮交互中的隐蔽语义漂移失效模式
可致模型夸大或隐瞒关键医学发现
现有安全评测未覆盖该风险
0ad7460e87bacd07b1f26da3ef2f2d2fdd3ea4d9.zh_abstract: 医学多模态大语言模型正越来越多地部署于高风险临床环境，然而当前的安全性评估在很大程度上忽略了一个关键失效模式：在临床上合理的多轮交互中累积的隐蔽语义漂移。此类漂移可使模型逐渐夸大或隐瞒关键医学发现，而不触发明确的安全机制。我们提出 MSIA（Medical Semantic Infiltration Attack，医学语义渗透攻击），一个用于在临床对话中建模并诱导多轮医学语义越狱的框架。MSIA 通过自适应策略选择和基于医学证据的闭环奖励反馈，能够在隐蔽约束下对累积语义漂移进行受控优化。基于胸部 X 射线（X-ray）的多模态医学对话实验显示，MSIA 始终优于现有越狱方法，覆盖 GPT-4o、

071f803c285c1dcfcbfdc73ffaca37ce52e9150a.title: FedMental: Evaluating Federated Learning for Mental Health Detection from Social Media Data
071f803c285c1dcfcbfdc73ffaca37ce52e9150a.abstract: Social media text data are often used to train Machine Learning (ML) models to identify users exhibiting high-risk mental health behaviors. However, sharing this sensitive data poses privacy risks and limits the growth of benchmark datasets. We comprehensively evaluate whether privacy-preserving ML techniques can enable safer data sharing while preserving performance. Specifically, we apply federated learning (FL) and Differentially Private FL for two widely-studied mental health prediction tasks: depression detection on X (Twitter) and suicide crisis detection on Reddit. We simulate realistic data-sharing scenarios by treating each user as a client in a non-IID setting, evaluating across different client fractions, aggregation strategies, and privacy budgets. While FL achieves comparable performance to centralized training (centralized F1 = 85.63; best FL model F1 = 83.16) on depression
071f803c285c1dcfcbfdc73ffaca37ce52e9150a.zh_title: FedMental：社交媒体心理健康检测的联邦学习评估
071f803c285c1dcfcbfdc73ffaca37ce52e9150a.summary: 系统评估联邦学习与差分隐私联邦学习在社交媒体心理健康风险识别任务中能否在保护隐私的同时保持性能。
key_points: 社交媒体文本常用于训练心理健康风险识别模型
数据共享受隐私风险并限制基准数据集发展
评估联邦学习与差分隐私联邦学习两类预测任务
071f803c285c1dcfcbfdc73ffaca37ce52e9150a.zh_abstract: 社交媒体文本数据常被用于训练机器学习（ML）模型，以识别表现出高风险心理健康行为的用户。然而，共享这些敏感数据会带来隐私风险，并限制基准数据集的发展。我们全面评估隐私保护机器学习技术能否在保持性能的同时实现更安全的数据共享。具体而言，我们针对两个被广泛研究的心理健康预测任务应用联邦学习（FL）和差分隐私联邦学习（Differentially Private FL）：X（Twitter）上的抑郁检测和 Reddit 上的自杀危机检测。我们通过将每个用户视为非独立同分布（non-IID）设置中的一个客户端来模拟现实的数据共享场景，并在不同的客户端比例、聚合策略和隐私预算下进行评估。虽然 FL 在抑郁检测上达到了与集中式训练相当的性能（集中式 F1 = 85.63；最佳 FL 模型 F1 = 83.16）

02a8754616318e424370de6901254e34e0794133.title: Cognitive Policy-Driven LLM for Diagnosis and Intervention of Cognitive Distortions in Emotional Support Conversation
02a8754616318e424370de6901254e34e0794133.abstract: Emotional Support Conversation (ESC) plays a critical role in mental health assistance by providing accessible psychological support in real-world applications. Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong empathetic abilities in ESC tasks. Yet, existing methods overlook the issue of cognitive distortions in help-seekers'expressions. As a result, current models can only provide basic emotional comfort, rather than helping help-seekers address their psychological distress at a deeper cognitive level. To address this challenge, we construct the CogBiasESC dataset, the first dataset that expands existing ESC datasets by adding labels for cognitive distortions, includes their type, intensity, and safe risk level. Furthermore, we propose the Cognitive Policy-driven Large Language Model framework (CoPoLLM) to enhance LLMs'ability to diagnose and intervene cognitive distortions in help-seeker
02a8754616318e424370de6901254e34e0794133.zh_title: 面向情绪支持对话中认知扭曲诊断与干预的认知策略驱动LLM
02a8754616318e424370de6901254e34e0794133.summary: 提出认知策略驱动的LLM方法，在情绪支持对话中诊断并干预求助者的认知扭曲，而非仅提供基础情绪安慰。
key_points: 情绪支持对话在心理健康援助中具重要作用
现有方法忽视求助者表达中的认知扭曲
当前模型多止于基础情绪安慰，未触及深层认知
02a8754616318e424370de6901254e34e0794133.zh_abstract: 情感支持对话（ESC）通过在实际应用中提供可及的心理支持，在心理健康援助中发挥关键作用。大语言模型（LLMs）在 ESC 任务中表现出很强的共情能力。然而，现有方法忽视了求助者表达中的认知扭曲问题。因此，当前模型只能提供基本的情绪安慰，而无法帮助求助者在更深层的认知层面应对其心理困扰。为应对这一挑战，我们构建了 CogBiasESC 数据集，这是首个通过添加认知扭曲标签来扩展现有 ESC 数据集的数据集，包含其类型、强度和安全风险等级。此外，我们提出了认知策略驱动的大语言模型框架（CoPoLLM），以增强 LLMs 诊断和干预求助者认知扭曲的能力。

00e3e65c37b08dbc80084838dd4db2bbf419bfc4.title: CURA: Clinical Uncertainty Risk Alignment for Language Model-Based Risk Prediction
00e3e65c37b08dbc80084838dd4db2bbf419bfc4.abstract: Clinical language models (LMs) are increasingly applied to support clinical risk prediction from free-text notes, yet their uncertainty estimates often remain poorly calibrated and clinically unreliable. In this work, we propose Clinical Uncertainty Risk Alignment (CURA), a framework that aligns clinical LM-based risk estimates and uncertainty with both individual error likelihoods and cohort-level ambiguities. CURA first fine-tunes domain-specific clinical LMs to obtain task-adapted patient embeddings, and then performs uncertainty fine-tuning of a multi-head classifier using a bi-level uncertainty objective. 00e3e65c37b08dbc80084838dd4db2bbf419bfc4.zh_title: CURA：语言模型临床风险预测的不确定性对齐
00e3e65c37b08dbc80084838dd4db2bbf419bfc4.summary: 提出CURA框架，将临床语言模型风险与不确定性同个体错误率和队列歧义对齐。
key_points: 临床语言模型不确定性校准不佳
对齐个体错误可能性与队列歧义
提升风险预测不确定性可靠性
00e3e65c37b08dbc80084838dd4db2bbf419bfc4.zh_abstract: 临床语言模型（LMs）正越来越多地被应用于支持基于自由文本笔记的临床风险预测，然而其不确定性估计往往校准不佳，且在临床上不可靠。在这项工作中，我们提出 Clinical Uncertainty Risk Alignment（CURA），一个使基于临床 LM 的风险估计和不确定性与个体错误可能性以及队列层面模糊性相一致的框架。CURA 首先微调领域特定的临床 LMs 以获得任务适配的患者嵌入，然后使用双层不确定性目标对多头分类器进行不确定性微调。具体而言，个体级校准项使预测不确定性与每位患者的错误可能性相一致，而队列感知正则化器将风险估计拉向其嵌入空间中局部邻域的事件率，并将额外权重放在模糊

910d26adcd83c4ec36f365198f8b2224b14ad6c9.title: MedHallu: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Detecting Medical Hallucinations in Large Language Models
910d26adcd83c4ec36f365198f8b2224b14ad6c9.abstract: Advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) and their increasing use in medical question-answering necessitate rigorous evaluation of their reliability. A critical challenge lies in hallucination, where models generate plausible yet factually incorrect outputs. In the medical domain, this poses serious risks to patient safety and clinical decision-making. To address this, we introduce MedHallu, the first benchmark specifically designed for medical hallucination detection. MedHallu comprises 10,000 high-quality question-answer pairs derived from PubMedQA, with hallucinated answers systematically generated through a controlled pipeline. Our experiments show that state-of-the-art LLMs, including GPT-4o, Llama-3.1, and the medically fine-tuned UltraMedical, struggle with this binary hallucination detection task, with the best model achieving an F1 score as low as 0.625 for detecting"hard"ca
910d26adcd83c4ec36f365198f8b2224b14ad6c9.zh_title: MedHallu：医学幻觉检测综合基准
910d26adcd83c4ec36f365198f8b2224b14ad6c9.summary: 提出首个面向医学幻觉检测的基准MedHallu，用于评估大模型医学问答的可靠性。
key_points: 医学幻觉威胁患者安全与临床决策
首个专门面向医学幻觉检测的基准
含1万条规模的数据构成
910d26adcd83c4ec36f365198f8b2224b14ad6c9.zh_abstract: 大型语言模型（Large Language Models, LLMs）的进步及其在医学问答中日益增多的应用，要求对其可靠性进行严格评估。一个关键挑战在于幻觉，即模型生成看似合理但事实上不正确的输出。在医学领域，这会对患者安全和临床决策构成严重风险。为解决这一问题，我们引入 MedHallu，这是首个专门为医学幻觉检测设计的基准。MedHallu 包含 10,000 个源自 PubMedQA 的高质量问答对，其中幻觉答案通过受控流程系统性地生成。我们的实验表明，包括 GPT-4o、Llama-3.1 和经医学微调的 UltraMedical 在内的最先进的 LLMs 在这一二元幻觉检测任务上表现吃力，最佳模型在检测“hard”ca方面实现了低至 0.625 的 F1 分数。

1fcfd53125b016aa47bbaffb0f6f0f1c85a09d77.title: Protein Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey
1fcfd53125b016aa47bbaffb0f6f0f1c85a09d77.abstract: Protein-specific large language models (Protein LLMs) are revolutionizing protein science by enabling more efficient protein structure prediction, function annotation, and design. While existing surveys focus on specific aspects or applications, this work provides the first comprehensive overview of Protein LLMs, covering their architectures, training datasets, evaluation metrics, and diverse applications. Through a systematic analysis of over 100 articles, we propose a structured taxonomy of state-of-the-art Protein LLMs, analyze how they leverage large-scale protein sequence data for improved accuracy, and explore their potential in advancing protein engineering and biomedical research. Additionally, we discuss key challenges and future directions, positioning Protein LLMs as essential tools for scientific discovery in protein science. Resources are maintained at https://github.com/Yij
1fcfd53125b016aa47bbaffb0f6f0f1c85a09d77.zh_title: 蛋白质大语言模型：综合综述
1fcfd53125b016aa47bbaffb0f6f0f1c85a09d77.summary: 系统综述蛋白质专用大语言模型，涵盖架构、训练数据集、评测指标与应用。
key_points: Protein LLM推动蛋白质结构预测、功能注释与设计

1fcfd53125b016aa47bbaffb0f6f0f1c85a09d77.zh_abstract: 蛋白质特异性大型语言模型（Protein LLMs）通过实现更高效的蛋白质结构预测、功能注释和设计，正在革新蛋白质科学。尽管现有综述聚焦于特定方面或应用，本工作提供了Protein LLMs的首个全面概述，涵盖其架构、训练数据集、评估指标和多样化应用。通过对100多篇文章的系统分析，我们提出了最先进Protein LLMs的结构化分类法，分析它们如何利用大规模蛋白质序列数据以提高准确性，并探索它们在推进蛋白质工程和生物医学研究方面的潜力。此外，我们讨论关键挑战和未来方向，将Protein LLMs定位为蛋白质科学中科学发现的重要工具。资源维护在 https://github.com/Yij

2a8cf14e036d451f27df981a8b2b7e039b96f89a.title: A Comprehensive Survey on the Trustworthiness of Large Language Models in Healthcare
2a8cf14e036d451f27df981a8b2b7e039b96f89a.abstract: The application of large language models (LLMs) in healthcare holds significant promise for enhancing clinical decision-making, medical research, and patient care. However, their integration into real-world clinical settings raises critical concerns around trustworthiness, particularly around dimensions of truthfulness, privacy, safety, robustness, fairness, and explainability. These dimensions are essential for ensuring that LLMs generate reliable, unbiased, and ethically sound outputs. While researchers have recently begun developing benchmarks and evaluation frameworks to assess LLM trustworthiness, the trustworthiness of LLMs in healthcare remains underexplored, lacking a systematic review that provides a comprehensive understanding and future insights. This survey addresses that gap by providing a comprehensive review of current methodologies and solutions aimed at mitigating risks
2a8cf14e036d451f27df981a8b2b7e039b96f89a.zh_title: 医疗健康大模型可信性综述
2a8cf14e036d451f27df981a8b2b7e039b96f89a.summary: 综述系统梳理医疗大模型在真实性、隐私、安全、鲁棒性、公平性与可解释性等可信维度的研究现状。
key_points: 大模型在临床决策与研究中应用前景广泛
真实临床部署面临可信性多重关切
围绕真实性、隐私、安全等维度展开梳理
2a8cf14e036d451f27df981a8b2b7e039b96f89a.zh_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）在医疗保健中的应用为增强临床决策、医学研究和患者护理带来了巨大希望。然而，将其整合到真实临床环境中会引发围绕可信度的关键担忧，尤其是在真实性、隐私、安全性、鲁棒性、公平性和可解释性等维度。这些维度对于确保 LLM 生成可靠、无偏见且符合伦理的输出至关重要。尽管研究人员最近已开始制定基准和评估框架来评估 LLM 的可信度，但 LLM 在医疗保健中的可信度仍未得到充分探索，缺乏能够提供全面理解和未来洞见的系统性综述。本综述通过全面回顾旨在减轻风险的当前方法和解决方案，填补了这一空白

799dcc2efd788f80770b6e829202642c5ca7e742.title: LLMEval-Med: A Real-world Clinical Benchmark for Medical LLMs with Physician Validation
799dcc2efd788f80770b6e829202642c5ca7e742.abstract: Evaluating large language models (LLMs) in medicine is crucial because medical applications require high accuracy with little room for error. Current medical benchmarks have three main types: medical exam-based, comprehensive medical, and specialized assessments. However, these benchmarks have limitations in question design (mostly multiple-choice), data sources (often not derived from real clinical scenarios), and evaluation methods (poor assessment of complex reasoning). To address these issues, we present LLMEval-Med, a new benchmark covering five core medical areas, including 2,996 questions created from real-world electronic health records and expert-designed clinical scenarios. We also design an automated evaluation pipeline, incorporating expert-developed checklists into our LLM-as-Judge framework. 799dcc2efd788f80770b6e829202642c5ca7e742.zh_title: LLMEval-Med：经医生验证的真实临床医学大模型基准
799dcc2efd788f80770b6e829202642c5ca7e742.summary: 提出基于真实临床场景并由医生验证的医学大模型评测基准，旨在改进题目设计、数据来源和复杂推理评估。
key_points: 现有医学基准多采用选择题设计
数据源常非真实临床场景
提出经医师验证的真实临床基准
799dcc2efd788f80770b6e829202642c5ca7e742.zh_abstract: 在医学中评估大型语言模型（LLM）至关重要，因为医学应用需要高准确性，几乎没有出错的空间。当前的医学基准主要有三种类型：基于医学考试的、综合医学的和专业评估。然而，这些基准在问题设计（大多是多项选择）、数据来源（通常并非来自真实临床场景）和评估方法（对复杂推理的评估不佳）方面存在局限性。为了解决这些问题，我们提出了 LLMEval-Med，一个涵盖五个核心医学领域的新基准，包括 2,996 个从真实世界电子健康记录和专家设计的临床场景中创建的问题。我们还设计了一个自动化评估流程，将专家开发的检查表纳入我们的 LLM-as-Judge 框架中。此外，我们的方法通过人机 agreem 验证机器评分

110ab0beb74ffb7ab1efe55ad36b4732835fa5c9.title: EmoAgent: Assessing and Safeguarding Human-AI Interaction for Mental Health Safety
110ab0beb74ffb7ab1efe55ad36b4732835fa5c9.abstract: The rise of LLM-driven AI characters raises safety concerns, particularly for vulnerable human users with psychological disorders. To address these risks, we propose EmoAgent, a multi-agent AI framework designed to evaluate and mitigate mental health hazards in human-AI interactions. EmoAgent comprises two components: EmoEval simulates virtual users, including those portraying mentally vulnerable individuals, to assess mental health changes before and after interactions with AI characters. It uses clinically proven psychological and psychiatric assessment tools (PHQ-9, PDI, PANSS) to evaluate mental risks induced by LLM. EmoGuard serves as an intermediary, monitoring users' mental status, predicting potential harm, and providing corrective feedback to mitigate risks. Experiments conducted in popular character-based chatbots show that emotionally engaging dialogues can lead to psychologic
110ab0beb74ffb7ab1efe55ad36b4732835fa5c9.zh_title: EmoAgent：评估与守护心理健康人机交互安全
110ab0beb74ffb7ab1efe55ad36b4732835fa5c9.summary: EMNLP 2025 提出多智能体框架 EmoAgent，用于评估与缓解人与 AI 角色交互中的心理健康风险。

EmoEval 模拟含心理脆弱人群的虚拟用户
对比交互前后心理健康变化
110ab0beb74ffb7ab1efe55ad36b4732835fa5c9.zh_abstract: LLM 驱动的 AI 角色的兴起引发了安全担忧，尤其是对患有心理障碍的脆弱人类用户。为应对这些风险，我们提出了 EmoAgent，一种多智能体 AI 框架，旨在评估并缓解人-AI 交互中的心理健康危害。EmoAgent 包含两个组件：EmoEval 模拟虚拟用户，包括那些扮演心理脆弱个体的用户，以评估与 AI 角色交互前后的心理健康变化。它使用经临床验证的心理与精神科评估工具（PHQ-9、PDI、PANSS）来评估由 LLM 引发的心理风险。EmoGuard 充当中间者，监测用户的心理状态，预测潜在伤害，并提供纠正性反馈以缓解风险。在流行角色型聊天机器人中进行的实验表明，情感投入的对话可导致心理

bddb021ee854256c521d1076d200f17b49052982.title: ReasonMed: A 370K Multi-Agent Generated Dataset for Advancing Medical Reasoning
bddb021ee854256c521d1076d200f17b49052982.abstract: Reasoning-based large language models have excelled in mathematics and programming, yet their potential in knowledge-intensive medical question answering remains underexplored and insufficiently validated in clinical contexts. To bridge this gap, we introduce ReasonMed, the largest medical reasoning dataset to date, comprising 370k high-quality examples distilled from 1.75 million initial reasoning paths generated by complementary LLMs and curated through a cost-efficient easy-medium-difficult (EMD) pipeline. ReasonMed is built through a multi-agent generation, verification, and refinement process, in which an Error Refiner improves reasoning paths by correcting error-prone steps identified by a verifier. bddb021ee854256c521d1076d200f17b49052982.zh_title: ReasonMed：37万条多智能体生成医学推理数据集
bddb021ee854256c521d1076d200f17b49052982.summary: EMNLP 2025发布迄今最大医学推理数据集ReasonMed，含37万条高质量样本。
key_points: 由互补大模型生成175万条初始推理路径
经易中难分层筛选得到37万条样本
面向知识密集型医学问答推理验证
bddb021ee854256c521d1076d200f17b49052982.zh_abstract: 基于推理的大语言模型在数学和编程方面表现出色，但它们在知识密集型医学问答中的潜力仍未得到充分探索，并且在临床情境中未得到充分验证。为弥合这一差距，我们提出 ReasonMed，这是迄今最大的医学推理数据集，包含 37 万个高质量示例，这些示例从由互补 LLM 生成的 175 万条初始推理路径中蒸馏而来，并通过成本高效的易-中-难（easy-medium-difficult, EMD）流程进行筛选。ReasonMed 通过多智能体生成、验证和精炼过程构建，其中 Error Refiner 通过纠正由验证器识别出的易错步骤来改进推理路径。利用 ReasonMed，我们研究了训练医学推理模型的有效策略，并发现将详细的 CoT 推理与简洁的答案摘要相结合能够产生最

1585c43b9c584854bcb42ce4e56416c6b3bc54f3.title: Med-PRM: Medical Reasoning Models with Stepwise, Guideline-verified Process Rewards
1585c43b9c584854bcb42ce4e56416c6b3bc54f3.abstract: Large language models have shown promise in clinical decision making, but current approaches struggle to localize and correct errors at specific steps of the reasoning process. This limitation is critical in medicine, where identifying and addressing reasoning errors is essential for accurate diagnosis and effective patient care. We introduce Med-PRM, a process reward modeling framework that leverages retrieval-augmented generation to verify each reasoning step against established medical knowledge bases. By verifying intermediate reasoning steps with evidence retrieved from clinical guidelines and literature, our model can precisely assess the reasoning quality in a fine-grained manner. Evaluations on five medical QA benchmarks and two open-ended diagnostic tasks demonstrate that Med-PRM achieves state-of-the-art performance, with improving the performance of base models by up to 13.50%
1585c43b9c584854bcb42ce4e56416c6b3bc54f3.zh_title: Med-PRM：基于指南验证式逐步过程奖励的医学推理模型
1585c43b9c584854bcb42ce4e56416c6b3bc54f3.summary: EMNLP 2025 论文提出 Med-PRM 过程奖励建模框架，利用检索增强生成对每一步推理按既有医学知识进行验证，以定位并纠正推理过程中的错误。
key_points: 现有方法难以定位并纠正具体推理步骤错误
医学场景中识别推理错误对诊疗至关重要
采用检索增强生成逐步核验医学知识
1585c43b9c584854bcb42ce4e56416c6b3bc54f3.zh_abstract: 大型语言模型在临床决策中已显示出前景，但当前方法难以在推理过程的特定步骤上定位和纠正错误。这一局限在医学中至关重要，因为识别和处理推理错误对于准确诊断和有效患者照护必不可少。我们介绍了 Med-PRM，一种过程奖励建模（process reward modeling）框架，其利用检索增强生成（retrieval-augmented generation）依据已确立的医学知识库验证每个推理步骤。通过用从临床指南和文献中检索到的证据验证中间推理步骤，我们的模型能够以细粒度方式精确评估推理质量。在五个医学 QA 基准和两个开放式诊断任务上的评估表明，Med-PRM 达到了最先进性能，并将基础模型的性能提升高达 13.50%

a7a2b307a05b8b4c5804e3c4601e0bd7381742c4.title: LIDDIA: Language-based Intelligent Drug Discovery Agent
a7a2b307a05b8b4c5804e3c4601e0bd7381742c4.abstract: Drug discovery is a long, expensive, and complex process, relying heavily on human medicinal chemists, who can spend years searching the vast space of potential therapies. Recent advances in artificial intelligence for chemistry have sought to expedite individual drug discovery tasks; however, there remains a critical need for an intelligent agent that can navigate the drug discovery process. Towards this end, we introduce LIDDiA, an autonomous agent capable of intelligently navigating the drug discovery process in silico. By leveraging the reasoning capabilities of large language models, LIDDiA serves as a low-cost and highly-adaptable tool for autonomous drug discovery. a7a2b307a05b8b4c5804e3c4601e0bd7381742c4.zh_title: LIDDiA：基于语言的智能药物发现智能体
a7a2b307a05b8b4c5804e3c4601e0bd7381742c4.summary: EMNLP 2025 提出 LIDDiA，可自主导航药物发现流程的智能体，以应对该过程耗时昂贵、依赖人类药物化学家的问题。
key_points: 自主智能体导航药物发现流程
针对药物发现耗时且昂贵的问题
基于语言与化学 AI 方法
a7a2b307a05b8b4c5804e3c4601e0bd7381742c4.zh_abstract: 药物发现是一个漫长、昂贵且复杂的过程，严重依赖人类药物化学家，他们可能花费数年时间搜索庞大的潜在疗法空间。近年来，化学人工智能的进展试图加速单个药物发现任务；然而，仍然迫切需要一种能够导航药物发现过程的智能体。为此，我们提出 LIDDiA，这是一种能够在计算机（in silico）中智能导航药物发现过程的自主智能体。通过利用大语言模型的推理能力，LIDDiA 可作为低成本且高度可适应的自主药物发现工具。我们全面检验了 LIDDiA，证明（1）它能在 30 个临床相关靶点中的超过 70% 上生成满足关键药物标准的分子，（2）它智能地平衡探索与 exploi

cd63455be2671968842016fecfbfbb5371331ddc.title: Agentic Medical Knowledge Graphs Enhance Medical Question Answering: Bridging the Gap Between LLMs and Evolving Medical Knowledge
cd63455be2671968842016fecfbfbb5371331ddc.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have significantly advanced medical question-answering by leveraging extensive clinical data and medical literature. However, the rapid evolution of medical knowledge and the labor-intensive process of manually updating domain-specific resources pose challenges to the reliability of these systems. To address this, we introduce Agentic Medical Graph-RAG (AMG-RAG), a comprehensive framework that automates the construction and continuous updating of medical knowledge graphs, integrates reasoning, and retrieves current external evidence, such as PubMed and WikiSearch. By dynamically linking new findings and complex medical concepts, AMG-RAG not only improves accuracy but also enhances interpretability in medical queries. cd63455be2671968842016fecfbfbb5371331ddc.zh_title: 智能体医学知识图谱增强医学问答
cd63455be2671968842016fecfbfbb5371331ddc.summary: 提出AMG-RAG框架，自动构建并持续更新医学知识图谱以增强大模型医学问答。
key_points: 医学知识快速演进影响系统可靠性
人工更新领域资源成本高
自动构建与持续更新知识图谱
cd63455be2671968842016fecfbfbb5371331ddc.zh_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）通过利用大量临床数据和医学文献，显著推动了医学问答的发展。然而，医学知识的快速演进以及手动更新领域特定资源的劳动密集型过程，对这些系统的可靠性构成了挑战。为解决这一问题，我们引入 Agentic Medical Graph-RAG（AMG-RAG），一个综合框架，可自动化医学知识图谱的构建与持续更新，整合推理，并检索当前外部证据，例如 PubMed 和 WikiSearch。通过动态链接新发现和复杂医学概念，AMG-RAG 不仅提高了准确性，还增强了医学查询中的可解释性。在 MEDQA 和 MEDMCQA 基准上的评估证明了 AMG-RAG 的有效性，在 MEDQA 上达到 74.1% 的 F1 分数，以及一个

cb228905345e0ccbcaab92cd0eebc02ade943ab6.title: RadEval: A framework for radiology text evaluation
cb228905345e0ccbcaab92cd0eebc02ade943ab6.abstract: We introduce RadEval, a unified, open-source framework for evaluating radiology texts. RadEval consolidates a diverse range of metrics, from classic n-gram overlap (BLEU, ROUGE) and contextual measures (BERTScore) to clinical concept-based scores (F1CheXbert, F1RadGraph, RaTEScore, SRR-BERT, TemporalEntityF1) and advanced LLM-based evaluators (GREEN). We refine and standardize implementations, extend GREEN to support multiple imaging modalities with a more lightweight model, and pretrain a domain-specific radiology encoder, demonstrating strong zero-shot retrieval performance. We also release a richly annotated expert dataset with over 450 clinically significant error labels and show how different metrics correlate with radiologist judgment. cb228905345e0ccbcaab92cd0eebc02ade943ab6.zh_title: RadEval：放射学文本评估统一框架
cb228905345e0ccbcaab92cd0eebc02ade943ab6.summary: EMNLP 2025 提出开源统一框架 RadEval，整合放射学文本的多种评估指标。
key_points: 涵盖 n-gram、上下文与临床概念类指标
含 LLM 评估器 GREEN，并做实现标准化
扩展 GREEN 支持多模态并采用更轻量模型
cb228905345e0ccbcaab92cd0eebc02ade943ab6.zh_abstract: 我们提出 RadEval，一个用于评估放射学文本的统一、开源框架。RadEval 整合了多样化的指标，从经典的 n-gram 重叠（BLEU、ROUGE）和上下文度量（BERTScore），到基于临床概念的评分（F1CheXbert、F1RadGraph、RaTEScore、SRR-BERT、TemporalEntityF1）以及先进的基于大语言模型的评估器（GREEN）。我们改进并标准化了实现，将 GREEN 扩展至支持多种成像模态并采用更轻量的模型，并预训练了一个领域特定的放射学编码器，展现出强大的零样本检索性能。我们还发布了一个标注丰富的专家数据集，包含 450 多个具有临床意义的错误标签，并展示了不同指标与放射科医生判断之间的相关性。最后，RadEval 提供了统计检验工具，并在多个公开可用数据集上给出基线模型评估，促进可复现

55acb9b8a70f4259ad58639fec9da7e57320bdd0.title: Ask Patients with Patience: Enabling LLMs for Human-Centric Medical Dialogue with Grounded Reasoning
55acb9b8a70f4259ad58639fec9da7e57320bdd0.abstract: The severe shortage of medical doctors limits access to timely and reliable healthcare, leaving millions underserved. Large language models (LLMs) offer a potential solution but struggle in real-world clinical interactions. Many LLMs are not grounded in authoritative medical guidelines and fail to transparently manage diagnostic uncertainty. Their language is often rigid and mechanical, lacking the human-like qualities essential for patient trust. To address these challenges, we propose Ask Patients with Patience (APP), a multi-turn LLM-based medical assistant designed for grounded reasoning, transparent diagnoses, and human-centric interaction. APP enhances communication by eliciting user symptoms through empathetic dialogue, significantly improving accessibility and user engagement. It also incorporates Bayesian active learning to support transparent and adaptive diagnoses. The framewo
55acb9b8a70f4259ad58639fec9da7e57320bdd0.zh_title: 以耐心问诊：人本医疗对话与有据推理
55acb9b8a70f4259ad58639fec9da7e57320bdd0.summary: EMNLP 2025提出Ask Pati（Ask Patients with Patience），使LLM依据权威指南开展人本化医疗对话。
key_points: 针对医生短缺与LLM临床交互不足
强调基于权威医学指南的有据推理
关注诊断不确定性与语言人性化
55acb9b8a70f4259ad58639fec9da7e57320bdd0.zh_abstract: 医生的严重短缺限制了对及时可靠医疗保健的可及性，使数百万人得不到充分服务。大型语言模型（LLMs）提供了一种潜在解决方案，但在真实世界临床互动中表现不佳。许多 LLMs 未以权威医学指南为依据，且未能透明地管理诊断不确定性。它们的语言往往生硬机械，缺乏患者信任所必需的类人特质。为应对这些挑战，我们提出 Ask Patients with Patience（APP），一个基于 LLM 的多轮医疗助手，旨在实现有依据的推理、透明的诊断和以人为本的交互。APP 通过共情对话引出用户症状来增强沟通，显著提高可及性和用户参与度。它还纳入贝叶斯主动学习，以支持透明且自适应的诊断。该框架

1c81bb341892f03e06aa7cfa6701f0d58b3d748b.title: Subtle Risks, Critical Failures: A Framework for Diagnosing Physical Safety of LLMs for Embodied Decision Making
1c81bb341892f03e06aa7cfa6701f0d58b3d748b.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for decision making in embodied agents, yet existing safety evaluations often rely on coarse success rates and domain-specific setups, making it difficult to diagnose why and where these models fail. This obscures our understanding of embodied safety and limits the selective deployment of LLMs in high-risk physical environments. We introduce SAFEL, the framework for systematically evaluating the physical safety of LLMs in embodied decision making. SAFEL assesses two key competencies: (1) rejecting unsafe commands via the Command Refusal Test, and (2) generating safe and executable plans via the Plan Safety Test. Critically, the latter is decomposed into functional modules, goal interpretation, transition modeling, action sequencing, enabling fine-grained diagnosis of safety failures. 0e7ccedbbb8492732ecf08901db44a81c7885c25.title: Large Language Models with Temporal Reasoning for Longitudinal Clinical Summarization and Prediction
0e7ccedbbb8492732ecf08901db44a81c7885c25.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have shown potential in clinical text summarization, but their ability to handle long patient trajectories with multi-modal data spread across time remains underexplored. This study systematically evaluates several state-of-the-art open-source LLMs, their Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) variants and chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting on long-context clinical summarization and prediction. We examine their ability to synthesize structured and unstructured Electronic Health Records (EHR) data while reasoning over temporal coherence, by re-engineering existing tasks, including discharge summarization and diagnosis prediction from two publicly available EHR datasets. Our results indicate that long context windows improve input integration but do not consistently enhance clinical reasoning, and LLMs are still struggling with temporal progressi
0e7ccedbbb8492732ecf08901db44a81c7885c25.zh_title: 面向纵向临床摘要与预测的时间推理大语言模型
0e7ccedbbb8492732ecf08901db44a81c7885c25.summary: 系统评测开源大模型、检索增强生成与思维链提示在长程多模态临床摘要与预测中的表现。
key_points: 系统评测多种开源大模型及其RAG与CoT变体
任务为跨时间多模态长程临床摘要与预测
长病程患者轨迹的处理能力仍待深入探索
0e7ccedbbb8492732ecf08901db44a81c7885c25.zh_abstract: 大语言模型（large language models, LLMs）的近期进展已显示出在临床文本摘要方面的潜力，但其处理跨时间分布的多模态数据所构成的长患者轨迹的能力仍未被充分探索。本研究系统评估了若干最先进的开源 LLMs、其检索增强生成（Retrieval Augmented Generation, RAG）变体以及思维链（chain-of-thought, CoT）提示在长上下文临床摘要和预测中的表现。我们通过重新设计现有任务，包括基于两个公开可用 EHR 数据集的出院摘要和诊断预测，考察它们在推理时间连贯性的同时综合结构化和非结构化电子健康记录（Electronic Health Records, EHR）数据的能力。我们的结果表明，长上下文窗口改善了输入整合，但并未一致增强临床推理，且 LLMs 仍在时间进展（temporal progressi）方面挣扎

8310a74ccd1a8032daccc978f5163dd83c961f25.title: Code Like Humans: A Multi-Agent Solution for Medical Coding
8310a74ccd1a8032daccc978f5163dd83c961f25.abstract: In medical coding, experts map unstructured clinical notes to alphanumeric codes for diagnoses and procedures. We introduce Code Like Humans: a new agentic framework for medical coding with large language models. It implements official coding guidelines for human experts, and it is the first solution that can support the full ICD-10 coding system (+70K labels). It achieves the best performance to date on rare diagnosis codes (fine-tuned discriminative classifiers retain an advantage for high-frequency codes, to which they are limited). Towards future work, we also contribute an analysis of system performance and identify its `blind spots'(codes that are systematically undercoded).
8310a74ccd1a8032daccc978f5163dd83c961f25.zh_title: Code Like Humans：多智能体医疗编码框架
8310a74ccd1a8032daccc978f5163dd83c961f25.summary: EMNLP 2025 提出基于大模型的智能体框架，按官方编码指南将临床文本映射为ICD-10编码，支持全部约7万标签。
key_points: 遵循官方人工编码指南
首次支持完整ICD-10编码体系
罕见诊断编码表现最佳
8310a74ccd1a8032daccc978f5163dd83c961f25.zh_abstract: 在医学编码中，专家将非结构化临床记录映射为用于诊断和操作的字母数字代码。我们提出 Code Like Humans：一种使用大语言模型进行医学编码的新智能体框架。它实现了面向人类专家的官方编码指南，并且是首个能够支持完整 ICD-10 编码系统（+70K 标签）的解决方案。它在罕见诊断代码上取得了迄今最佳性能（微调的判别式分类器在高频代码上仍保持优势，而它们仅限于高频代码）。面向未来工作，我们还贡献了对系统性能的分析，并识别出其“盲点”（被系统性编码不足的代码）。

f704d289a3a1075ded47e554f2dc08466dd64107.title: From Scores to Steps: Diagnosing and Improving LLM Performance in Evidence-Based Medical Calculations
f704d289a3a1075ded47e554f2dc08466dd64107.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated promising performance on medical benchmarks; however, their ability to perform medical calculations, a crucial aspect of clinical decision-making, remains underexplored and poorly evaluated. Existing benchmarks often assess only the final answer with a wide numerical tolerance, overlooking systematic reasoning failures and potentially causing serious clinical misjudgments. In this work, we revisit medical calculation evaluation with a stronger focus on clinical trustworthiness. First, we clean and restructure the MedCalc-Bench dataset and propose a new step-by-step evaluation pipeline that independently assesses formula selection, entity extraction, and arithmetic computation. f704d289a3a1075ded47e554f2dc08466dd64107.zh_title: 从分数到步骤：诊断并改进LLM的循证医学计算
f704d289a3a1075ded47e554f2dc08466dd64107.summary: 重新审视医学计算评测，关注推理过程而非仅最终答案，以诊断并改进大模型表现。
key_points: 现有基准仅看最终答案且数值容差过宽
忽视系统性推理失败或致临床误判
重新设计医学计算的评测方式
f704d289a3a1075ded47e554f2dc08466dd64107.zh_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）在医学基准测试中表现出有前景的性能；然而，它们执行医学计算的能力——临床决策的一个关键方面——仍然未被充分探索且评估不足。现有基准通常仅以较宽的数值容差评估最终答案，忽视了系统性推理失败，并可能导致严重的临床误判。在这项工作中，我们重新审视医学计算评估，更加关注临床可信度。首先，我们清理并重构了MedCalc-Bench数据集，并提出了一种新的逐步评估流程，该流程独立评估公式选择、实体提取和算术计算。在这个细粒度框架下，GPT-4o的准确率从62.7%下降到43.6%，揭示了先前评估所掩盖的错误。其次，我们引入了一种自动错误

40252c9440ca7450f5a15156d2116fc3981127f2.title: RGAR: Recurrence Generation-augmented Retrieval for Factual-aware Medical Question Answering
40252c9440ca7450f5a15156d2116fc3981127f2.abstract: Medical question answering requires extensive access to specialized conceptual knowledge. The current paradigm, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), acquires expertise medical knowledge through large-scale corpus retrieval and uses this knowledge to guide a general-purpose large language model (LLM) for generating answers. However, existing retrieval approaches often overlook the importance of factual knowledge, which limits the relevance of retrieved conceptual knowledge and restricts its applicability in real-world scenarios, such as clinical decision-making based on Electronic Health Records (EHRs). This paper introduces RGAR, a recurrence generation-augmented retrieval framework that retrieves both relevant factual and conceptual knowledge from dual sources (i.e., EHRs and the corpus), allowing them to interact and refine each another. 40252c9440ca7450f5a15156d2116fc3981127f2.zh_title: RGAR：面向事实感知医学问答的生成增强检索

b4d051579e765d453d8a1ce2ff32f7a131d9248e.title: 3MDBench: Medical Multimodal Multi-agent Dialogue Benchmark
b4d051579e765d453d8a1ce2ff32f7a131d9248e.abstract: Though Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) are being actively explored in medicine, their ability to conduct complex real-world telemedicine consultations combining accurate diagnosis with professional dialogue remains underexplored. This paper presents 3MDBench (Medical Multimodal Multi-agent Dialogue Benchmark), an open-source framework for simulating and evaluating LVLM-driven telemedical consultations. 3MDBench simulates patient variability through temperament-based Patient Agent and evaluates diagnostic accuracy and dialogue quality via Assessor Agent. It includes 2996 cases across 34 diagnoses from real-world telemedicine interactions, combining textual and image-based data. ef9678b094c7ad6ae6efa1ed587731b19f4fb5cd.title: Empowering Healthcare Practitioners with Language Models: Structuring Speech Transcripts in Two Real-World Clinical Applications
ef9678b094c7ad6ae6efa1ed587731b19f4fb5cd.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) such as GPT-4o and o1 have demonstrated strong performance on clinical natural language processing (NLP) tasks across multiple medical benchmarks. Nonetheless, two high-impact NLP tasks - structured tabular reporting from nurse dictations and medical order extraction from doctor-patient consultations - remain underexplored due to data scarcity and sensitivity, despite active industry efforts. Practical solutions to these real-world clinical tasks can significantly reduce the documentation burden on healthcare providers, allowing greater focus on patient care. In this paper, we investigate these two challenging tasks using private and open-source clinical datasets, evaluating the performance of both open- and closed-weight LLMs, and analyzing their respective strengths and limitations. Furthermore, we propose an agentic pipeline for generating realistic, non-s
ef9678b094c7ad6ae6efa1ed587731b19f4fb5cd.zh_title: 语言模型用于真实临床语音转写结构化任务

ef9678b094c7ad6ae6efa1ed587731b19f4fb5cd.zh_abstract: 如 GPT-4o 和 o1 之类的大语言模型（Large Language Models, LLMs）已在多个医学基准的临床自然语言处理（natural language processing, NLP）任务上展现出强劲性能。尽管如此，两项高影响力的 NLP 任务——根据护士口述生成结构化表格报告，以及从医患问诊中提取医嘱——由于数据稀缺和敏感性，仍未被充分探索，尽管业界已有积极努力。针对这些真实世界临床任务的实用解决方案可以显著减轻医疗提供者的文书负担，使其能够更专注于患者照护。在本文中，我们使用私有和开源临床数据集研究这两项具有挑战性的任务，评估开放权重和闭权重 LLM 的性能，并分析它们各自的优势与局限。此外，我们提出一种代理式流水线，用于生成逼真、非敏感

cf927d5a0044eb56d203335949067c69c8184a45.title: Trustworthy Medical Question Answering: An Evaluation-Centric Survey
cf927d5a0044eb56d203335949067c69c8184a45.abstract: Trustworthiness in healthcare question-answering (QA) systems is important for ensuring patient safety, clinical effectiveness, and user confidence. As large language models (LLMs) become increasingly integrated into medical settings, the reliability of their responses directly influences clinical decision-making and patient outcomes. However, achieving comprehensive trustworthiness in medical QA poses significant challenges due to the inherent complexity of healthcare data, the critical nature of clinical scenarios, and the multifaceted dimensions of trustworthy AI. In this survey, we systematically examine six key dimensions of trustworthiness in medical QA, i.e., Factuality, Robustness, Fairness, Safety, Explainability, and Calibration. cf927d5a0044eb56d203335949067c69c8184a45.zh_abstract: 医疗保健问答（QA）系统中的可信度对于确保患者安全、临床有效性和用户信心非常重要。随着大语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地集成到医疗环境中，其响应的可靠性直接影响临床决策和患者结果。然而，由于医疗数据的固有复杂性、临床场景的关键性质以及可信AI的多方面维度，在医学QA中实现全面的可信度面临重大挑战。在这篇综述中，我们系统地考察了医学QA中可信度的六个关键维度，即事实性（Factuality）、鲁棒性（Robustness）、公平性（Fairness）、安全性（Safety）、可解释性（Explainability）和校准性（Calibration）。我们回顾了在现有的基于LLM的医学QA系统中每个维度是如何被评估的。我们汇编并比较了旨在评估这些 d 的主要基准。

66f9a84c44e147fdad9d983a0ca52d9284ee17f2.title: AUTOCT: Automating Interpretable Clinical Trial Prediction with LLM Agents
66f9a84c44e147fdad9d983a0ca52d9284ee17f2.abstract: Clinical trials are critical for advancing medical treatments but remain prohibitively expensive and time-consuming. Accurate prediction of clinical trial outcomes can significantly reduce research and development costs and accelerate drug discovery. While recent deep learning models have shown promise by leveraging unstructured data, their black-box nature, lack of interpretability, and vulnerability to label leakage limit their practical use in high-stakes biomedical contexts. In this work, we propose AutoCT, a novel framework that combines the reasoning capabilities of large language models with the explainability of classical machine learning. AutoCT autonomously generates, evaluates, and refines tabular features based on public information without human input. 66f9a84c44e147fdad9d983a0ca52d9284ee17f2.zh_title: AUTOCT：用LLM智能体自动化可解释临床试验预测

1395b448abbd77a8d7ff1bac04d09b92e5f61269.title: Assessing and Mitigating Medical Knowledge Drift and Conflicts in Large Language Models
1395b448abbd77a8d7ff1bac04d09b92e5f61269.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have great potential in the field of health care, yet they face great challenges in adapting to rapidly evolving medical knowledge. This can lead to outdated or contradictory treatment suggestions. This study investigated how LLMs respond to evolving clinical guidelines, focusing on concept drift and internal inconsistencies. We developed the DriftMedQA benchmark to simulate guideline evolution and assessed the temporal reliability of various LLMs. Our evaluation of seven state-of-the-art models across 4,290 scenarios demonstrated difficulties in rejecting outdated recommendations and frequently endorsing conflicting guidance. Additionally, we explored two mitigation strategies: Retrieval-Augmented Generation and preference fine-tuning via Direct Preference Optimization. 1395b448abbd77a8d7ff1bac04d09b92e5f61269.zh_title: 评估与缓解大语言模型的医学知识漂移与冲突

1395b448abbd77a8d7ff1bac04d09b92e5f61269.zh_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）在医疗保健领域具有巨大潜力，但它们在适应快速发展的医学知识方面面临巨大挑战。这可能导致过时或矛盾的治疗建议。本研究调查了 LLMs 如何响应不断演变的临床指南，重点关注概念漂移和内部不一致性。我们开发了 DriftMedQA 基准来模拟指南演变，并评估了各种 LLMs 的时间可靠性。我们对七种最先进模型在 4,290 个场景中的评估表明，它们在拒绝过时建议方面存在困难，并经常认可相互矛盾的指导。此外，我们探索了两种缓解策略：检索增强生成（Retrieval-Augmented Generation）和通过直接偏好优化（Direct Preference Optimization）进行偏好微调。虽然每种方法都提高了模型性能，但它们的组合带来了最一致的

da985d14eb39c71e18b35410afd844a4e5693e41.title: How Real Are Synthetic Therapy Conversations? Evaluating Fidelity in Prolonged Exposure Dialogues
da985d14eb39c71e18b35410afd844a4e5693e41.abstract: Synthetic data adoption in healthcare is driven by privacy concerns, data access limitations, and high annotation costs. We explore synthetic Prolonged Exposure (PE) therapy conversations for PTSD as a scalable alternative for training clinical models. We systematically compare real and synthetic dialogues using linguistic, structural, and protocol-specific metrics like turn-taking and treatment fidelity. We introduce and evaluate PE-specific metrics, offering a novel framework for assessing clinical fidelity beyond surface fluency. Our findings show that while synthetic data successfully mitigates data scarcity and protects privacy, capturing the most subtle therapeutic dynamics remains a complex challenge. da985d14eb39c71e18b35410afd844a4e5693e41.zh_title: 合成治疗对话有多真实？延长暴露对话保真度评估

c9e40759be37d6b3d0883e79c283249380e7f852.title: Knowledge-enhanced Multimodal ECG Representation Learning with Arbitrary-Lead Inputs
c9e40759be37d6b3d0883e79c283249380e7f852.abstract: Recent advances in multimodal ECG representation learning center on aligning ECG signals with paired free-text reports. However, suboptimal alignment persists due to the complexity of medical language and the reliance on a full 12-lead setup, which is often unavailable in under-resourced settings. To tackle these issues, we propose **K-MERL**, a knowledge-enhanced multimodal ECG representation learning framework. **K-MERL** leverages large language models to extract structured knowledge from free-text reports and employs a lead-aware ECG encoder with dynamic lead masking to accommodate arbitrary lead inputs. Evaluations on six external ECG datasets show that **K-MERL** achieves state-of-the-art performance in zero-shot classification and linear probing tasks, while delivering an average **16%** AUC improvement over existing methods in partial-lead zero-shot classification.

c9e40759be37d6b3d0883e79c283249380e7f852.zh_abstract: 多模态心电图（ECG）表示学习的最新进展集中于将ECG信号与配对的自由文本报告对齐。然而，由于医学语言的复杂性以及对完整12导联设置的依赖，对齐效果仍不理想；而在资源匮乏的环境中，完整12导联设置往往无法获得。为解决这些问题，我们提出**K-MERL**，一个知识增强的多模态ECG表示学习框架。**K-MERL**利用大语言模型从自由文本报告中提取结构化知识，并采用具有动态导联掩码的导联感知ECG编码器，以适应任意导联输入。在六个外部ECG数据集上的评估表明，**K-MERL**在零样本分类和线性探测任务中取得了最先进的性能，同时在部分导联零样本分类中比现有方法平均提升**16%**的AUC。

ba1e5a5461774480a591340ee105f3e044240a87.title: Elucidating Mechanisms of Demographic Bias in LLMs for Healthcare
ba1e5a5461774480a591340ee105f3e044240a87.abstract: We know from prior work that LLMs encode social biases, and that this manifests in clinical tasks. In this work we adopt tools from mechanistic interpretability to unveil sociodemographic representations and biases within LLMs in the context of healthcare. Specifically, we ask: Can we identify activations within LLMs that encode sociodemographic information (e.g., gender, race)? We find that gender information is highly localized in MLP layers and can be reliably manipulated at inference time via patching. Such interventions can surgically alter generated clinical vignettes for specific conditions, and also influence downstream clinical predictions which correlate with gender, e.g., patient risk of depression. ba1e5a5461774480a591340ee105f3e044240a87.zh_abstract: 我们从先前工作中知道，大语言模型（LLMs）会编码社会偏见，并且这会在临床任务中显现。在这项工作中，我们采用机制可解释性工具，在医疗保健背景下揭示LLM内部的社会人口统计学表征和偏见。具体而言，我们问：我们能否识别LLM中编码社会人口统计学信息（例如性别、种族）的激活？我们发现性别信息高度集中在MLP层中，并且可以在推理时通过修补可靠地操纵。此类干预可以精准改变针对特定疾病生成的临床情景案例，也会影响与性别相关的下游临床预测，例如患者抑郁风险。我们发现患者种族的表征在某种程度上更为分散，但也可以在一定程度上进行干预。据我们所知，这是机制…的首次应用

60405001f4b8ded61c2bb2f9b64e170dd2dc0fa3.title: MedFact: A Large-scale Chinese Dataset for Evidence-based Medical Fact-checking of LLM Responses
60405001f4b8ded61c2bb2f9b64e170dd2dc0fa3.abstract: Medical fact-checking has become increasingly critical as more individuals seek medical information online. However, existing datasets predominantly focus on human-generated content, leaving the verification of content generated by large language models (LLMs) relatively unexplored. To address this gap, we introduce MedFact, the first evidence-based Chinese medical fact-checking dataset of LLM-generated medical content. It consists of 1,321 questions and 7,409 claims, mirroring the complexities of real-world medical scenarios. We conduct comprehensive experiments in both in-context learning (ICL) and fine-tuning settings, showcasing the capability and challenges of current LLMs on this task, accompanied by an in-depth error analysis to point out key directions for future research. Our dataset is publicly available at https://github.com/AshleyChenNLP/MedFact.

60405001f4b8ded61c2bb2f9b64e170dd2dc0fa3.zh_abstract: 随着越来越多的人在线上寻求医疗信息，医学事实核查已变得日益关键。然而，现有数据集主要关注人类生成的内容，使得对大型语言模型（LLMs）生成内容的验证相对未被探索。为填补这一空白，我们提出了 MedFact，这是首个基于证据的、针对 LLM 生成医学内容的中文医学事实核查数据集。它包含 1,321 个问题和 7,409 条声明，反映了真实世界医学场景的复杂性。我们在上下文学习（ICL）和微调两种设置下进行了全面实验，展示了当前 LLMs 在该任务上的能力与挑战，并辅以深入的错误分析，以指出未来研究的关键方向。我们的数据集公开可用，地址为 https://github.com/AshleyChenNLP/MedFact。

b934506667c543abd32ce9dd27b739d9eb19bb0c.abstract: Accurate clinical coding is essential for healthcare documentation, billing, and decision-making. While prior work shows that off-the-shelf LLMs struggle with this task, evaluations based on exact match metrics often overlook errors where predicted codes are hierarchically close but incorrect. Our analysis reveals that such hierarchical misalignments account for a substantial portion of LLM failures. We show that lightweight interventions, including prompt engineering and small-scale fine-tuning, can improve accuracy without the computational overhead of search-based methods. To address hierarchically near-miss errors, we introduce clinical code verification as both a standalone task and a pipeline component. 6530be9dce96386acb79a5d27ecf517b4f4e07b5.title: SuPreME: A Supervised Pre-training Framework for Multimodal ECG Representation Learning
6530be9dce96386acb79a5d27ecf517b4f4e07b5.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Electrocardiogram (ECG) is critical for diagnosing and monitoring cardiac health, but obtaining large-scale annotated ECG datasets is labor-intensive and time-consuming. Recent ECG Self-Supervised Learning (eSSL) methods mitigate this by learning features without extensive labels but fail to capture fine-grained clinical semantics and require extensive task-specific fine-tuning. To address these challenges, we propose $\textbf{SuPreME}$, a $\textbf{Su}$pervised $\textbf{Pre}$-training framework for $\textbf{M}$ultimodal $\textbf{E}$CG representation learning. 62b7fa550c5af54211db695c00d64ed15dee556e.abstract: Discharge communication is a critical yet underexplored component of patient care, where the goal shifts from diagnosis to education. While recent large language model (LLM) benchmarks emphasize in-visit diagnostic reasoning, they fail to evaluate models’ ability to support patients after the visit. 194828ad6317272dda3d7966e86f7549e33f5eef.title: Causal Representation Learning from Multimodal Clinical Records under Non-Random Modality Missingness
194828ad6317272dda3d7966e86f7549e33f5eef.abstract: Clinical notes contain rich patient information, such as diagnoses or medications, making them valuable for patient representation learning. Recent advances in large language models have further improved the ability to extract meaningful representations from clinical texts. However, clinical notes are often missing. f8d35eb644443ec356e594f96c0b6454ffc6590d.title: Not What the Doctor Ordered: Surveying LLM-based De-identification and Quantifying Clinical Information Loss
f8d35eb644443ec356e594f96c0b6454ffc6590d.abstract: De-identification in the healthcare setting is an application of NLP where automated algorithms are used to remove personally identifying information of patients (and, sometimes, providers). With the recent rise of generative large language models (LLMs), there has been a corresponding rise in the number of papers that apply LLMs to de-identification. Although these approaches often report near-perfect results, significant challenges concerning reproducibility and utility of the research papers persist. This paper identifies three key limitations in the current literature: inconsistent reporting metrics hindering direct comparisons, the inadequacy of traditional classification metrics in capturing errors which LLMs may be more prone to (i.e., altering clinically relevant information), and lack of manual validation of automated metrics which aim to quantify these errors. f8d35eb644443ec356e594f96c0b6454ffc6590d.zh_title: LLM 去标识化综述：量化临床信息损失

bfcb3998ad89e61699fc45a5f099e916eaceb2c7.title: A Knowledge-driven Adaptive Collaboration of LLMs for Enhancing Medical Decision-making
bfcb3998ad89e61699fc45a5f099e916eaceb2c7.abstract: Medical decision-making often involves integrating knowledge from multiple clinical specialties, typically achieved through multidisciplinary teams. Inspired by this collaborative process, recent work has leveraged large language models (LLMs) in multi-agent collaboration frameworks to emulate expert teamwork. While these approaches improve reasoning through agent interaction, they are limited by static, pre-assigned roles, which hinder adaptability and dynamic knowledge integration. To address these limitations, we propose KAMAC, a Knowledge-driven Adaptive Multi-Agent Collaboration framework that enables LLM agents to dynamically form and expand expert teams based on the evolving diagnostic context. bfcb3998ad89e61699fc45a5f099e916eaceb2c7.zh_title: 知识驱动的LLM自适应协作提升医疗决策

a1408bfa829144b16d38c48c456d014e3e00d8c9.title: No Black Boxes: Interpretable and Interactable Predictive Healthcare with Knowledge-Enhanced Agentic Causal Discovery
a1408bfa829144b16d38c48c456d014e3e00d8c9.abstract: Deep learning models trained on extensive Electronic Health Records (EHR) data have achieved high accuracy in diagnosis prediction, offering the potential to assist clinicians in decision-making and treatment planning. However, these models lack two crucial features that clinicians highly value: interpretability and interactivity. The ``black-box''nature of these models makes it difficult for clinicians to understand the reasoning behind predictions, limiting their ability to make informed decisions. Additionally, the absence of interactive mechanisms prevents clinicians from incorporating their own knowledge and experience into the decision-making process. a1408bfa829144b16d38c48c456d014e3e00d8c9.zh_title: 知识增强智能体因果发现：可解释可交互的EHR预测

8270b8d8dd71bfbb366b3bf52c166fd3341ae38a.title: Factuality Beyond Coherence: Evaluating LLM Watermarking Methods for Medical Texts
8270b8d8dd71bfbb366b3bf52c166fd3341ae38a.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are adapted to sensitive domains such as medicine, their fluency raises safety risks, particularly regarding provenance and accountability. Watermarking embeds detectable patterns to mitigate these risks, yet its reliability in medical contexts remains untested. Existing benchmarks focus on detection-quality tradeoffs and overlook factual risks. In medical text, watermarking often reweights low-entropy tokens, which are highly predictable and often carry critical medical terminology. Shifting these tokens can cause inaccuracy and hallucinations, risks that prior general-domain benchmarks fail to capture. We propose a medical-focused evaluation workflow that jointly assesses factual accuracy and coherence. 8270b8d8dd71bfbb366b3bf52c166fd3341ae38a.zh_abstract: 随着大语言模型（LLMs）被适配到医学等敏感领域，其流畅性带来了安全风险，尤其是在来源溯源与问责方面。水印通过嵌入可检测的模式来缓解这些风险，但其在医学语境中的可靠性仍未得到检验。现有基准关注检测质量之间的权衡，而忽视了事实性风险。在医学文本中，水印往往会重新加权低熵词元（token），这些词元高度可预测，且常常承载关键的医学术语。改变这些词元可能导致不准确和幻觉，而这些风险是先前通用领域基准无法捕捉的。我们提出了一个以医学为重点的评估工作流程，联合评估事实准确性和连贯性。使用 GPT-Judger 并进一步进行人工验证，我们引入了事实性加权分数（Factuality-Weighted Score, FWS），这是一种将事实准确性置于优先地位、超越……的复合指标

5ed877ee3a7f32af225661200516020fa1534c5f.title: ReDepress: A Cognitive Framework for Detecting Depression Relapse from Social Media
5ed877ee3a7f32af225661200516020fa1534c5f.abstract: Almost 50% depression patients face the risk of going into relapse. The risk increases to 80% after the second episode of depression. Although, depression detection from social media has attained considerable attention, depression relapse detection has remained largely unexplored due to the lack of curated datasets and the difficulty of distinguishing relapse and non-relapse users. In this work, we present ReDepress, the first clinically validated social media dataset focused on relapse, comprising 204 Reddit users annotated by mental health professionals. Unlike prior approaches, our framework draws on cognitive theories of depression, incorporating constructs such as attention bias, interpretation bias, memory bias and rumination into both annotation and modeling. Through statistical analyses and machine learning experiments, we demonstrate that cognitive markers significantly differen
5ed877ee3a7f32af225661200516020fa1534c5f.zh_title: ReDepress：社交媒体抑郁症复发检测认知框架
5ed877ee3a7f32af225661200516020fa1534c5f.summary: 提出首个经临床验证的社交媒体抑郁症复发数据集与检测框架ReDepress，应对复发检测数据稀缺与用户区分难题。
key_points: 近50%抑郁症患者面临复发风险
第二次发作后风险升至80%
发布首个经临床验证的复发社交媒体数据集
5ed877ee3a7f32af225661200516020fa1534c5f.zh_abstract: 几乎 50% 的抑郁症患者面临复发风险。在第二次抑郁发作后，该风险增至 80%。尽管从社交媒体进行抑郁检测已获得相当多关注，但由于缺乏经过整理的数据集以及区分复发与非复发用户的难度，抑郁复发检测在很大程度上仍未得到探索。在这项工作中，我们提出 ReDepress，首个经临床验证、聚焦复发的社交媒体数据集，包含由心理健康专业人员标注的 204 名 Reddit 用户。与先前方法不同，我们的框架借鉴抑郁症认知理论，将注意偏向、解释偏向、记忆偏向和反刍等构念纳入标注和建模。通过统计分析和机器学习实验，我们证明认知标记显著不同

447101bf2b9aa22037fa624dc561a7cd119ff8ed.title: Rethinking Text-based Protein Understanding: Retrieval or LLM?
447101bf2b9aa22037fa624dc561a7cd119ff8ed.abstract: In recent years, protein-text models have gained significant attention for their potential in protein generation and understanding. Current approaches focus on integrating protein-related knowledge into large language models through continued pretraining and multi-modal alignment, enabling simultaneous comprehension of textual descriptions and protein sequences. Through a thorough analysis of existing model architectures and text-based protein understanding benchmarks, we identify significant data leakage issues present in current benchmarks. Moreover, conventional metrics derived from natural language processing fail to accurately assess the model's performance in this domain. To address these limitations, we reorganize existing datasets and introduce a novel evaluation framework based on biological entities. 447101bf2b9aa22037fa624dc561a7cd119ff8ed.zh_title: 重新思考基于文本的蛋白质理解：检索还是LLM？
447101bf2b9aa22037fa624dc561a7cd119ff8ed.summary: EMNLP 2025论文，分析基于文本的蛋白质理解现有模型与基准，探讨检索与LLM路径。
key_points: 分析蛋白质-文本模型架构
指出现有基准存在不足
比较检索与LLM方法
447101bf2b9aa22037fa624dc561a7cd119ff8ed.zh_abstract: 近年来，蛋白质-文本模型因其在蛋白质生成与理解方面的潜力而受到显著关注。当前的方法专注于通过持续预训练和多模态对齐，将蛋白质相关知识整合到大语言模型中，从而能够同时理解文本描述和蛋白质序列。通过对现有模型架构和基于文本的蛋白质理解基准的深入分析，我们发现当前基准中存在显著的数据泄漏问题。此外，源自自然语言处理的传统指标无法准确评估模型在该领域的表现。为解决这些局限，我们重新组织了现有数据集，并引入了一个基于生物实体的新评估框架。受我们观察结果的启发，我们提出了一种检索增强的方法，该方法……

42c50fa673658c4651022f623a09627b126ea627.title: How to Make Large Language Models Generate 100% Valid Molecules?
42c50fa673658c4651022f623a09627b126ea627.abstract: Molecule generation is key to drug discovery and materials science, enabling the design of novel compounds with specific properties. Large language models (LLMs) can learn to perform a wide range of tasks from just a few examples. However, generating valid molecules using representations like SMILES is challenging for LLMs in few-shot settings. In this work, we explore how LLMs can generate 100% valid molecules. We evaluate whether LLMs can use SELFIES, a representation where every string corresponds to a valid molecule, for valid molecule generation but find that LLMs perform worse with SELFIES than with SMILES. We then examine LLMs'ability to correct invalid SMILES and find their capacity limited. Finally, we introduce SmiSelf, a cross-chemical language framework for invalid SMILES correction. SmiSelf converts invalid SMILES to SELFIES using grammatical rules, leveraging SELFIES'mechan
42c50fa673658c4651022f623a09627b126ea627.zh_title: 如何让大语言模型生成100%合法分子？
42c50fa673658c4651022f623a09627b126ea627.summary: EMNLP 2025探讨LLM少样本生成合法分子的挑战，并评估其对SELFIES等表示的可用性。
key_points: 少样本下LLM生成SMILES合法分子困难
探索实现100%合法分子的途径
评估LLM是否可使用SELFIES表示
42c50fa673658c4651022f623a09627b126ea627.zh_abstract: 分子生成是药物发现和材料科学的关键，能够设计具有特定性质的新型化合物。大型语言模型（LLMs）可以仅从少量示例中学会执行广泛任务。然而，在少样本设置下，使用 SMILES 等表示生成有效分子对 LLM 具有挑战性。在这项工作中，我们探索 LLM 如何生成 100% 有效的分子。我们评估 LLM 是否可以使用 SELFIES（一种每个字符串都对应一个有效分子的表示）进行有效分子生成，但发现 LLM 使用 SELFIES 的表现比使用 SMILES 更差。然后，我们检查 LLM 纠正无效 SMILES 的能力，发现其能力有限。最后，我们提出 SmiSelf，一个用于无效 SMILES 纠正的跨化学语言框架。SmiSelf 使用语法规则将无效 SMILES 转换为 SELFIES，利用 SELFIES 的机制

313a406ceb1c06d71cab6cd896ecf845ad195b12.title: "What's Up, Doc?": Analyzing How Users Seek Health Information in Large-Scale Conversational AI Datasets
313a406ceb1c06d71cab6cd896ecf845ad195b12.abstract: People are increasingly seeking healthcare information from large language models (LLMs) via interactive chatbots, yet the nature and inherent risks of these conversations remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we filter large-scale conversational AI datasets to achieve HealthChat-11K, a curated dataset of 11K real-world conversations composed of 25K user messages. We use HealthChat-11K and a clinician-driven taxonomy for how users interact with LLMs when seeking healthcare information in order to systematically study user interactions across 21 distinct health specialties. Our analysis reveals insights into the nature of how and why users seek health information, such as common interactions, instances of incomplete context, affective behaviors, and interactions (e.g., leading questions) that can induce sycophancy, underscoring the need for improvements in the healthcare support capab
313a406ceb1c06d71cab6cd896ecf845ad195b12.zh_title: “怎么了，医生？”：分析用户在大规模对话AI中寻求健康信息
313a406ceb1c06d71cab6cd896ecf845ad195b12.summary: 该研究构建HealthChat-11K数据集，分析用户通过对话AI寻求健康信息的行为。
key_points: 人们日益通过LLM聊天机器人获取健康信息
构建含1.1万真实对话、2.5万用户消息数据集
基于临床医生分类法分析用户交互方式
313a406ceb1c06d71cab6cd896ecf845ad195b12.zh_abstract: 人们越来越多地通过交互式聊天机器人从大型语言模型（LLMs）获取医疗保健信息，然而这些对话的性质和固有风险在很大程度上仍未被探索。在本文中，我们过滤大规模对话式 AI 数据集，构建了 HealthChat-11K，这是一个包含 11K 真实世界对话、由 25K 用户消息组成的精选数据集。我们使用 HealthChat-11K 以及一个由临床医生驱动的分类体系（用于描述用户在寻求医疗保健信息时如何与 LLMs 交互），系统性地研究跨 21 个不同健康专科的用户交互。我们的分析揭示了关于用户如何以及为何寻求健康信息的性质的洞见，例如常见交互、不完整上下文的情形、情感行为，以及可能诱导谄媚的交互（例如，诱导性问题），凸显了改进医疗保健支持 capab 的必要性。

2874cba89249c19d4cb57603505dfc2a7dfe5bfc.title: MedEBench: Diagnosing Reliability in Text-Guided Medical Image Editing
2874cba89249c19d4cb57603505dfc2a7dfe5bfc.abstract: Text-guided image editing has seen significant progress in natural image domains, but its application in medical imaging remains limited and lacks standardized evaluation frameworks. Such editing could revolutionize clinical practices by enabling personalized surgical planning, enhancing medical education, and improving patient communication. To bridge this gap, we introduce MedEBench1, a robust benchmark designed to diagnose reliability in text-guided medical image editing. MedEBench consists of 1,182 clinically curated image-prompt pairs covering 70 distinct editing tasks and 13 anatomical regions. It contributes in three key areas: (1) a clinically grounded evaluation framework that measures Editing Accuracy, Context Preservation, and Visual Quality, complemented by detailed descriptions of intended edits and corresponding Region-of-Interest (ROI) masks; (2) a comprehensive comparison
2874cba89249c19d4cb57603505dfc2a7dfe5bfc.zh_title: MedEBench：诊断文本引导医学图像编辑可靠性
2874cba89249c19d4cb57603505dfc2a7dfe5bfc.summary: EMNLP 2025 Findings 提出 MedEBench 基准，用于诊断文本引导医学图像编辑的可靠性。
key_points: 文本引导图像编辑在医学领域应用有限
该领域缺乏标准化评估框架
MedEBench 为诊断可靠性提供基准
2874cba89249c19d4cb57603505dfc2a7dfe5bfc.zh_abstract: 文本引导的图像编辑在自然图像领域已取得显著进展，但其在医学影像中的应用仍然有限，且缺乏标准化评估框架。此类编辑可以通过实现个性化手术规划、增强医学教育以及改善患者沟通来彻底改变临床实践。为弥合这一差距，我们提出了 MedEBench1，一个稳健的基准，旨在诊断文本引导的医学图像编辑的可靠性。MedEBench 包含 1,182 个临床精选的图像-提示对，覆盖 70 个不同的编辑任务和 13 个解剖区域。它在三个关键方面作出贡献：（1）一个临床基础评估框架，衡量编辑准确性、上下文保持和视觉质量，并辅以对预期编辑的详细描述和相应的感兴趣区域（ROI）掩膜；（2）一项全面比较

2198a46ff2110ae50aac4a8428642823188d260c.title: ReEvalMed: Rethinking Medical Report Evaluation by Aligning Metrics with Real-World Clinical Judgment
2198a46ff2110ae50aac4a8428642823188d260c.abstract: Automatically generated radiology reports often receive high scores from existing evaluation metrics but fail to earn clinicians'trust. This gap reveals fundamental flaws in how current metrics assess the quality of generated reports. We rethink the design and evaluation of these metrics and propose a clinically grounded Meta-Evaluation framework. We define clinically grounded criteria spanning clinical alignment and key metric capabilities, including discrimination, robustness, and monotonicity. Using a fine-grained dataset of ground truth and rewritten report pairs annotated with error types, clinical significance labels, and explanations, we systematically evaluate existing metrics and reveal their limitations in interpreting clinical semantics, such as failing to distinguish clinically significant errors, over-penalizing harmless variations, and lacking consistency across error sever
2198a46ff2110ae50aac4a8428642823188d260c.zh_title: ReEvalMed：以真实临床判断对齐医学报告评价指标
2198a46ff2110ae50aac4a8428642823188d260c.summary: 作者反思医学报告自动评价指标，提出以临床为基础的元评价框架，涵盖临床一致性与区分度、鲁棒性、单调性等能力。
key_points: 指出现有指标高分但难获临床医生信任
提出临床基础的元评价框架
界定临床一致性与关键指标能力标准
2198a46ff2110ae50aac4a8428642823188d260c.zh_abstract: 自动生成的放射学报告往往在现有评估指标下获得高分，却无法赢得临床医生的信任。这一差距揭示了当前指标在评估生成报告质量方面存在的根本缺陷。我们重新思考这些指标的设计与评估，并提出了一个基于临床的元评估（Meta-Evaluation）框架。我们定义了具有临床依据的标准，涵盖临床对齐以及关键指标能力，包括区分度、鲁棒性和单调性。利用一个细粒度数据集——包含带有错误类型、临床意义标签和解释标注的真实报告与改写报告配对——我们系统评估了现有指标，并揭示了它们在解读临床语义方面的局限，例如无法区分具有临床意义的错误、对无害变体过度惩罚，以及在错误严重程度……缺乏一致性

08ee14dad60b0f36d4e2f10449eaee4d30ef43d0.title: Facts Fade Fast: Evaluating Memorization of Outdated Medical Knowledge in Large Language Models
08ee14dad60b0f36d4e2f10449eaee4d30ef43d0.abstract: The growing capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) show significant potential to enhance healthcare by assisting medical researchers and physicians. However, their reliance on static training data is a major risk when medical recommendations evolve with new research and developments. When LLMs memorize outdated medical knowledge, they can provide harmful advice or fail at clinical reasoning tasks. To investigate this problem, we introduce two novel question-answering (QA) datasets derived from systematic reviews: MedRevQA (16,501 QA pairs covering general biomedical knowledge) and MedChangeQA (a subset of 512 QA pairs where medical consensus has changed over time). Our evaluation of eight prominent LLMs on the datasets reveals consistent reliance on outdated knowledge across all models. We additionally analyze the influence of obsolete pre-training data and training strategies to e
08ee14dad60b0f36d4e2f10449eaee4d30ef43d0.zh_title: Facts Fade Fast：评估大模型对过时医学知识的记忆
08ee14dad60b0f36d4e2f10449eaee4d30ef43d0.summary: EMNLP 2025 构建两个问答数据集，评估大语言模型对过时医学知识的记忆及其在临床推理中的风险。
key_points: 指出静态训练数据带来的风险
引入两个医学问答数据集
关注过时知识导致的有害建议
08ee14dad60b0f36d4e2f10449eaee4d30ef43d0.zh_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）不断增强的能力显示出通过协助医学研究人员和医生来提升医疗保健的巨大潜力。然而，当医学建议随着新的研究与发展而演变时，它们对静态训练数据的依赖是一个重大风险。当 LLMs 记忆过时的医学知识时，它们可能提供有害建议或在临床推理任务中失败。为研究这一问题，我们引入了两个源自系统综述的新型问答（QA）数据集：MedRevQA（16,501 个问答对，涵盖一般生物医学知识）和 MedChangeQA（512 个问答对的子集，其中医学共识随时间发生了变化）。我们在这些数据集上对八个知名 LLMs 的评估显示，所有模型都一致地依赖过时知识。我们还分析了过时的预训练数据和训练策略的影响，以……

d3e6ae1a390b97f678c906cb6b964e065e20e815.title: MultiMed-ST: Large-scale Many-to-many Multilingual Medical Speech Translation
d3e6ae1a390b97f678c906cb6b964e065e20e815.abstract: Multilingual speech translation (ST) and machine translation (MT) in the medical domain enhances patient care by enabling efficient communication across language barriers, alleviating specialized workforce shortages, and facilitating improved diagnosis and treatment, particularly during pandemics. In this work, we present the first systematic study on medical ST, to our best knowledge, by releasing MultiMed-ST, a large-scale ST dataset for the medical domain, spanning all translation directions in five languages: Vietnamese, English, German, French, and Simplified/Traditional Chinese, together with the models. With 290,000 samples, this is the largest medical MT dataset and the largest many-to-many multilingual ST among all domains. Secondly, we present the most comprehensive ST analysis in the field's history, to our best knowledge, including: empirical baselines, bilingual-multilingual
d3e6ae1a390b97f678c906cb6b964e065e20e815.zh_title: MultiMed-ST：大规模多对多医疗语音翻译数据集
d3e6ae1a390b97f678c906cb6b964e065e20e815.summary: 发布首个大规模医疗领域语音翻译数据集MultiMed-ST，覆盖全部翻译方向，并开展医疗语音翻译的系统性研究。
key_points: 首个系统性医疗语音翻译研究
数据集覆盖所有翻译方向
面向跨语言医患沟通场景
d3e6ae1a390b97f678c906cb6b964e065e20e815.zh_abstract: 医疗领域的多语言语音翻译（ST）和机器翻译（MT）通过实现跨语言障碍的高效沟通、缓解专业劳动力短缺以及促进诊断和治疗的改进（尤其是在大流行病期间），从而提升患者护理水平。在本工作中，据我们所知，我们通过发布 MultiMed-ST（一个面向医疗领域的大规模 ST 数据集，涵盖五种语言：越南语、英语、德语、法语和简体/繁体中文的所有翻译方向，并附带模型），首次对医疗 ST 进行了系统性研究。该数据集包含 290,000 个样本，是最大的医疗 MT 数据集，也是所有领域中最大的多对多多语言 ST。其次，据我们所知，我们提出了该领域历史上最全面的 ST 分析，包括：经验基线、双语-多语言

c78cd7b4b0ee6a3fdd632be70232dfcfd285b583.title: Chatbot To Help Patients Understand Their Health
c78cd7b4b0ee6a3fdd632be70232dfcfd285b583.abstract: Patients must possess the knowledge necessary to actively participate in their care. We present NoteAid-Chatbot, a conversational AI that promotes patient understanding via a novel ‘learning as conversation’ framework, built on a multi-agent large language model (LLM) and reinforcement learning (RL) setup without human-labeled data. NoteAid-Chatbot was built on a lightweight 3B-parameter LLaMA 3.2 model trained in two stages: initial supervised fine-tuning on conversational data synthetically generated using medical conversation strategies, followed by RL with rewards derived from patient understanding assessments in simulated hospital discharge scenarios. Our evaluation, which includes comprehensive human-aligned assessments and case studies, demonstrates that NoteAid-Chatbot exhibits key emergent behaviors critical for patient education—such as clarity, relevance, and structured dialog
c78cd7b4b0ee6a3fdd632be70232dfcfd285b583.zh_title: NoteAid-Chatbot：帮助患者理解健康信息
c78cd7b4b0ee6a3fdd632be70232dfcfd285b583.summary: 基于多智能体LLM与强化学习的对话式AI，采用无人工标注的“以对话学习”框架帮助患者理解健康信息。
key_points: 多智能体LLM与强化学习结合

c78cd7b4b0ee6a3fdd632be70232dfcfd285b583.zh_abstract: 患者必须掌握积极参与自身护理所需的知识。我们提出了 NoteAid-Chatbot，一种通过新颖的‘对话即学习’框架促进患者理解的对话式 AI，它基于多智能体大型语言模型（LLM）和强化学习（RL）设置构建，无需人工标注数据。NoteAid-Chatbot 基于轻量级 30 亿参数 LLaMA 3.2 模型构建，分两个阶段训练：首先在使用医学对话策略合成生成的对话数据上进行初始监督微调，然后进行 RL，其奖励来自模拟医院出院场景中的患者理解评估。我们的评估包括全面的人类对齐评估和案例研究，表明 NoteAid-Chatbot 表现出对患者教育至关重要的关键涌现行为——例如清晰性、相关性和结构化对话

5a02b00c2354acbf2144d8e12a0ac37c883677d9.title: FT-MDT: Extracting Decision Trees from Medical Texts via a Novel Low-rank Adaptation Method
5a02b00c2354acbf2144d8e12a0ac37c883677d9.abstract: Knowledge of the medical decision process, which can be modeled as medical decision trees (MDTs), is critical to building clinical decision support systems. However, current MDT construction methods rely heavily on time-consuming and laborious manual annotation. To address this challenge, we propose PI-LoRA (Path-Integrated LoRA), a novel low-rank adaptation method for automatically extracting MDTs from clinical guidelines and textbooks. We integrate gradient path information to capture synergistic effects between different modules, enabling more effective and reliable rank allocation. This framework ensures that the most critical modules receive appropriate rank allocations while less important ones are pruned, resulting in a more efficient and accurate model for extracting medical decision trees from clinical texts. 5a02b00c2354acbf2144d8e12a0ac37c883677d9.zh_title: FT-MDT：用低秩适配从医学文本提取决策树

3909c57b2da1d542e8fadb1fb83f520638cb2009.title: M3Retrieve: Benchmarking Multimodal Retrieval for Medicine
3909c57b2da1d542e8fadb1fb83f520638cb2009.abstract: With the increasing use of RetrievalAugmented Generation (RAG), strong retrieval models have become more important than ever. In healthcare, multimodal retrieval models that combine information from both text and images offer major advantages for many downstream tasks such as question answering, cross-modal retrieval, and multimodal summarization, since medical data often includes both formats. However, there is currently no standard benchmark to evaluate how well these models perform in medical settings. To address this gap, we introduce M3Retrieve, a Multimodal Medical Retrieval Benchmark. M3Retrieve, spans 5 domains,16 medical fields, and 4 distinct tasks, with over 1.2 Million text documents and 164K multimodal queries, all collected under approved licenses. 3909c57b2da1d542e8fadb1fb83f520638cb2009.zh_abstract: 随着检索增强生成（RAG）的使用日益增多，强大的检索模型变得比以往任何时候都更重要。在医疗保健中，结合文本和图像信息的多模态检索模型对许多下游任务（如问答、跨模态检索和多模态摘要）具有重大优势，因为医疗数据通常包含两种格式。然而，目前还没有标准基准来评估这些模型在医疗环境中的表现。为了填补这一空白，我们介绍M3Retrieve，一个多模态医学检索基准。M3Retrieve涵盖5个领域、16个医学领域和4个不同任务，拥有超过120万个文本文档和16.4万个多模态查询，全部在经批准的许可下收集。我们在此基准上评估领先的多模态检索模型，以探索不同医学专科特有的挑战

291d7063a0bfa77b960181044995e0560508270e.title: Africa Health Check: Probing Cultural Bias in Medical LLMs
291d7063a0bfa77b960181044995e0560508270e.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in global healthcare, yet their outputs often reflect Western-centric training data and omit indigenous medical systems and region-specific treatments. This study investigates cultural bias in instruction-tuned medical LLMs using a curated dataset of African traditional herbal medicine. We evaluate model behavior across two complementary tasks, namely, multiple-choice questions and fill-in-the-blank completions, designed to capture both treatment preferences and responsiveness to cultural context. To quantify outcome preferences and prompt influences, we apply two complementary metrics: Cultural Bias Score (CBS) and Cultural Bias Attribution (CBA). 291d7063a0bfa77b960181044995e0560508270e.zh_title: 非洲健康检查：探查医学大模型的文化偏见
291d7063a0bfa77b960181044995e0560508270e.summary: 以非洲传统草药数据集评估指令微调医学大模型的文化偏见，涵盖选择题与填空任务。

291d7063a0bfa77b960181044995e0560508270e.zh_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）正越来越多地部署于全球医疗保健中，然而其输出往往反映以西方为中心的训练数据，并忽略本土医疗系统和区域特定治疗。本研究利用一个精心整理的非洲传统草药医学数据集，调查了经过指令调优的医疗 LLM 中的文化偏见。我们在两个互补任务上评估模型行为，即多项选择题和填空补全，旨在捕捉治疗偏好和对文化背景的响应能力。为了量化结果偏好和提示影响，我们应用两个互补指标：文化偏见分数（CBS）和文化偏见归因（CBA）。我们的结果表明，虽然提示适应可以减少固有偏见并增强文化一致性，但模型对上下文指导的响应程度各不相同。持续默认

0ab74266e48101bc842de39be4db46e8b4a43c59.title: TracSum: A New Benchmark for Aspect-Based Summarization with Sentence-Level Traceability in Medical Domain
0ab74266e48101bc842de39be4db46e8b4a43c59.abstract: While document summarization with LLMs has enhanced access to textual information, concerns about the factual accuracy of these summaries persist, especially in the medical domain. Tracing evidence from which summaries are derived enables users to assess their accuracy, thereby alleviating this concern. In this paper, we introduce TracSum, a novel benchmark for traceable, aspect-based summarization, in which generated summaries are paired with sentence-level citations, enabling users to trace back to the original context. First, we annotate 500 medical abstracts for seven key medical aspects, yielding 3.5K summary-citation pairs. We then propose a fine-grained evaluation framework for this new task, designed to assess the completeness and consistency of generated content using four metrics. 0ab74266e48101bc842de39be4db46e8b4a43c59.zh_title: TracSum：医学领域句级可溯源方面摘要基准
0ab74266e48101bc842de39be4db46e8b4a43c59.summary: 研究提出TracSum基准，为医学领域方面摘要提供句级引用溯源，便于用户核查摘要的事实准确性。
key_points: LLM摘要事实准确性在医学领域受关注

0ab74266e48101bc842de39be4db46e8b4a43c59.zh_abstract: 虽然使用 LLM 进行文档摘要增强了对文本信息的获取，但人们对其摘要事实准确性的担忧仍然存在，尤其是在医疗领域。追溯摘要所依据的证据使用户能够评估其准确性，从而减轻这种担忧。在本文中，我们介绍了 TracSum，一个用于可追溯、基于方面的摘要的新基准，其中生成的摘要与句子级引用配对，使用户能够追溯回原始上下文。首先，我们为七个关键医疗方面标注了 500 篇医疗摘要，产生了 3.5K 个摘要-引用对。然后，我们为这项新任务提出了一个细粒度评估框架，旨在使用四个指标评估生成内容的完整性和一致性。最后，我们介绍了一个摘要流水线 Track-Then-Sum，它作为一种基线方法

e50509fea8c0af8fe5698a13f911500be40d0a5d.title: Reframe Your Life Story: Interactive Narrative Therapist and Innovative Moment Assessment with Large Language Models
e50509fea8c0af8fe5698a13f911500be40d0a5d.abstract: Recent progress in large language models (LLMs) has opened new possibilities for mental health support, yet current approaches lack realism in simulating specialized psychotherapy and fail to capture therapeutic progression over time. Narrative therapy, which helps individuals transform problematic life stories into empowering alternatives, remains underutilized due to limited access and social stigma. We address these limitations through a comprehensive framework with two core components. First, INT (Interactive Narrative Therapist) simulates expert narrative therapists by planning therapeutic stages, guiding reflection levels, and generating contextually appropriate expert-like responses. e50509fea8c0af8fe5698a13f911500be40d0a5d.zh_title: 用大语言模型重构生命故事：交互式叙事治疗与创新时刻评估
e50509fea8c0af8fe5698a13f911500be40d0a5d.summary: 论文构建结合大语言模型的叙事治疗框架，用于模拟专业心理治疗并评估治疗过程中的创新时刻与进展。

e50509fea8c0af8fe5698a13f911500be40d0a5d.zh_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）的近期进展为心理健康支持开辟了新的可能性，但当前方法在模拟专门心理治疗时缺乏真实感，并且未能捕捉随时间推移的治疗进展。叙事治疗帮助个体将有问题的生活故事转化为赋权性的替代故事，但由于可及性有限和社会污名，仍未得到充分利用。我们通过一个包含两个核心组成部分的综合框架来应对这些局限。首先，INT（Interactive Narrative Therapist，互动叙事治疗师）通过规划治疗阶段、引导反思层级并生成符合情境的类专家回应，来模拟专家叙事治疗师。其次，IMA（Innovative Moment Assessment，创新时刻评估）提供一种以治疗为中心的评估方法，通过追踪“创新时刻”（Innovative Moments，IMs）——来访者言语中关键的叙事转变——来量化有效性。

e08590352647a03aa3440737b988ac9e546383c3.title: DrKGC: Dynamic Subgraph Retrieval-Augmented LLMs for Knowledge Graph Completion across General and Biomedical Domains
e08590352647a03aa3440737b988ac9e546383c3.abstract: Knowledge graph completion (KGC) aims to predict missing triples in knowledge graphs (KGs) by leveraging existing triples and textual information. Recently, generative large language models (LLMs) have been increasingly employed for graph tasks. However, current approaches typically encode graph context in textual form, which fails to fully exploit the potential of LLMs for perceiving and reasoning about graph structures. To address this limitation, we propose DrKGC (Dynamic Subgraph Retrieval-Augmented LLMs for Knowledge Graph Completion). DrKGC employs a flexible lightweight model training strategy to learn structural embeddings and logical rules within the KG. It then leverages a novel bottom-up graph retrieval method to extract a subgraph for each query guided by the learned rules. e08590352647a03aa3440737b988ac9e546383c3.zh_title: DrKGC：动态子图检索增强LLM的知识图谱补全
e08590352647a03aa3440737b988ac9e546383c3.summary: 提出DrKGC，以动态子图检索增强大语言模型，在通用与生物医学领域完成知识图谱补全。

e08590352647a03aa3440737b988ac9e546383c3.zh_abstract: 知识图谱补全（KGC）旨在利用已有三元组和文本信息来预测知识图谱（KGs）中缺失的三元组。近来，生成式大型语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被用于图任务。然而，当前方法通常以文本形式编码图上下文，未能充分发挥 LLMs 感知和推理图结构的潜力。为解决这一局限，我们提出 DrKGC（Dynamic Subgraph Retrieval-Augmented LLMs for Knowledge Graph Completion，用于知识图谱补全的动态子图检索增强 LLMs）。DrKGC 采用灵活的轻量级模型训练策略来学习 KG 中的结构嵌入和逻辑规则。随后，它利用一种新颖的自底向上图检索方法，在学习到的规则引导下为每个查询抽取一个子图。最后，图卷积网络（GCN）适配器使用检索到的子图来增强结构。

6ec5fe52cdc5c950f937ac8d587739fe47fc1eea.abstract: The learning process for medical residents presents significant challenges, demanding both the ability to interpret complex case reports and the rapid acquisition of accurate medical knowledge from reliable sources. Residents typically study case reports and engage in discussions with peers and mentors, but finding relevant educational materials and evidence to support their learning from these cases is often time-consuming and challenging. To address this, we introduce MedTutor, a novel system designed to augment resident training by automatically generating evidence-based educational content and multiple-choice questions from clinical case reports. MedTutor leverages a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline that takes clinical case reports as input and produces targeted educational materials. 6ec5fe52cdc5c950f937ac8d587739fe47fc1eea.zh_title: MedTutor：面向病例教学的检索增强大模型系统

6136642fddb96155f65a36ae9e1dd579b4b8bb56.title: From Feedback to Checklists: Grounded Evaluation of AI-Generated Clinical Notes
6136642fddb96155f65a36ae9e1dd579b4b8bb56.abstract: AI-generated clinical notes are increasingly used in healthcare, but evaluating their quality remains a challenge due to high subjectivity and limited scalability of expert review. Existing automated metrics often fail to align with real-world physician preferences. Using deidentified data from over 21,000 clinical encounters (prepared in accordance with the HIPAA safe harbor standard) from a deployed AI medical scribe system, we show that our feedback-derived checklist outperforms a baseline approach in our offline evaluations in coverage, diversity, and predictive power for human ratings. 5b9bed6a5f0c643c6217d5cec8a89cdb64aa1f2a.title: MADD: Multi-Agent Drug Discovery Orchestra
5b9bed6a5f0c643c6217d5cec8a89cdb64aa1f2a.abstract: Hit identification is a central challenge in early drug discovery, traditionally requiring substantial experimental resources. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, particularly large language models (LLMs), have enabled virtual screening methods that reduce costs and improve efficiency. Multi-agent systems offer a promising solution by combining the interpretability of LLMs with the precision of specialized models and tools. In this work, we present MADD, a multi-agent system that builds and executes customized hit identification pipelines from natural language queries.
